messages.author: e4181d5c40fc094c
messages.subject: methylKit read() issue
parts:
Hi Altuna,

I am working on new dataset. This is a test run and is having low CpG coverage (ranges from 1 to 60).

>head (test1.txt)
chrBase chr base strand coverage freqC freqT
chr1.10494 chr1 10494 R 1 0 100
chr1.10498 chr1 10498 R 1 100 0
chr1.10526 chr1 10526 R 1 0 100
chr1.10543 chr1 10543 R 1 0 100
chr1.13504 chr1 13504 R 1 0 100

When I read the above file into methylKit, I get an error as follows:
> read("test1.txt","test1","hg19")
Error in scan(file, what, nmax, sep, dec, quote, skip, nlines, na.strings,  : 
  scan() expected 'an integer', got '33.3333'

After trying to find out the problem, I noticed that after 200 lines there is a CpG with freqC =33.33. 

chr1.771963     chr1    771963  R       3       33.3333 66.6667

Actually it should not be a problem. Somehow methylKit didn't accept 'real number' in this case. It seems that methylKit derives the class information for each column of the data by reading few lines at the beginning and assumes that every entry follows the same pattern. Here in my case the first few lines are integers and real numbers come later. This seems to result in error (I rectified this by replacing an integer with a 'real number' in the first CpG of the file, then it worked)

How about defining the class information while performing scan() rather than allowing methylkit to assess class?


Regards,
Kalyan

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: methylKit read() issue
parts:
Hi Kalyan,
if you add ".0" on the to the fist row and fregC and fregT columns, the function will correctly think those are numeric values, since the function reads first couple of hundred lines and decides classes,
alternatively you can try the new mread() function I'm working on. It is faster and doesn't have this problem, https://gist.github.com/al2na/6e47cf0a084ecfbd3075

# load the mread function and methylKit
library(methylKit)
library(devtools)
source_gist("6e47cf0a084ecfbd3075")

file.list=list( system.file("extdata", "test1.myCpG.txt", package = "methylKit"),
                system.file("extdata", "test2.myCpG.txt", package = "methylKit"),
                system.file("extdata", "control1.myCpG.txt", package = "methylKit"),
                system.file("extdata", "control2.myCpG.txt", package = "methylKit") )

# read the files to a methylRawList object: myobj
myobj=mread( file.list,
            sample.id=list("test1","test2","ctrl1","ctrl2"),assembly="hg18",treatment=c(1,1,0,0))

myobj2=mread( file.list[[1]],sample.id="test1",assembly="hg18")




Usage is similar to the read() function:

mread(location,sample.id,assembly,pipeline="amp",header=T,skip=0,sep="\t",context="CpG",resolution="base",treatment)
